question.problem:
If the midpoint of the line segment with endpoints $(7,-4)$ and $(a,b)$ is $(2,1),$
then $a+b=$
question.worked_solution:
The given points are ${{(7,-4)}_{⏟}}_{\text{(}{x}_{1},\,{y}_{1})},$ ${{(a,b)}_{⏟}}_{\text{(}{x}_{2},\,{y}_{2})}$ and ${{(2,1)}_{⏟}}_{\text{(}{x}_{m},\,{y}_{m})}\,.$

We use the midpoint formula as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}({x}_{m},{y}_{m}) & =(\frac{{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}}{2},\frac{{y}_{1}+{y}_{2}}{2}) \\ (2,1) & =(\frac{7+a}{2},\frac{-4+b}{2}).\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding $x$- and $y$-coordinates in the equation above gives us

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}2=\frac{7+a}{2} \\ 1=\frac{-4+b}{2}\end{aligned}\,⇒\,{\begin{aligned}a=-3 \\ b=6.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, $(a,b)=(-3,6)$ and $a+b=3.$
